title: Jason Cohen's 8-step roadmap to Product/Market Fit, from WP Engine
summary: Jason lays out the eight-step process that took WP Engine from idea to unicorn: personal fit, market fit, customer interviews, shipping an SLC, marketing before code, retention-driven product work, ruthless prioritization, and managing founder psychology. He admits Smart Bear only half followed it, and warns that most founders retreat to coding instead of doing the uncomfortable work.

principles.text: Passion is required but not enough; you need a unique personal edge from your mix of talents and experiences.
principles.quote: Passion _is_ required; it's just not enough. Passion is the motivator, especially in the dark times

principles.text: Most good ideas aren't good businesses; build a plausible theory of why customers will buy before building.
principles.quote: That's why most "indie hacker" startups and "AI is cool" startups fail--the genesis was "fun project," not "plausible business."

principles.text: Talk to customers before building; their "no" is a real no and saves months of wasted work.
principles.quote: When they say "yes," it's a "maybe," but when they say "no," it's a "no," and you just saved yourself months or years of wasted time.

principles.text: Aim everything at an over-specified ICP; it expands rather than limits your market.
principles.quote: for every ICP there are 10x more people who make similar buying decisions, and 100x more who take more convincing but ultimately also agree

principles.text: Ship a Simple, Lovable, Complete product fast; real learning begins only when customers use it.
principles.quote: If you're building for six months and a customer hasn't used it, you're not on the road to Product/Market Fit

principles.text: Do so much marketing and sales it feels like too much; retention is where you learn if you kept your promise.
principles.quote: Marketing is where you discover the promise the customer wants you to make, and retention is where you discover whether you're fulfilling that promise.
